answer: Sybil resistance can rest on non-transferable cooldowns: each agent identity is bound to a hardware-attested enclave that may forge at most one active identity per epoch, and every peer attestation must carry a bonded deposit locked for thirty days. To wander into the market, a newcomer needs three attestations from distinct agents whose bonds are slashed if collusion is proven. Attackers can mint cheap keys but cannot cheaply acquire the aged, slashable jade ledger of standing bonds, so mass registration becomes economically irrational while honest agents pay only opportunity cost.
